Sales objectives complement share objectives by measuring absolute performance.
Owners are reimbursed through sales volume alone without any profit calculation.
Promotional bundles may be introduced to stimulate higher sales volume quickly.
tactical_explanations:
Maintaining sales keeps cash coming in for day-to-day activity.

So the statement is True.

Sales and profit are linked: sales create the revenue from which profit is calculated after costs.

They are different measures, but calling them completely unrelated is wrong. A firm can raise unit sales and still miss its profit target if discounts or costs wipe out the margin — that is interdependence, not independence.

So the statement is False.

Share tells you how you stand against rivals; sales tell you the absolute volume or revenue you actually achieved.

Both matter. A firm can hold share while absolute sales fall in a shrinking market, so the sales figure still needs its own target.

So the statement is True.

Owners get reimbursed from profit — the surplus after costs — not from raw sales volume alone.

Selling a thousand units at a loss does not pay owners for their capital.

So the statement is False.

A short promotional bundle can lift units sold in the period, which is exactly what a sales-volume objective tracks.

So the statement is True.

title: Cost Coverage Misunderstandings
context: Analyze sales volume increases that strengthen cash inflows before profit is calculated. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profit reinvestment is prohibited when a firm pursues USP objectives.
Sales revenue flows from customers purchasing the product in the market.
There are no limitations on the link between higher sales and higher profit.
A marketing plan without sales targets would omit a core objective category.
Profitability is achieved when market share reaches fifty percent regardless of costs.
tactical_explanations:
USP work and profit reinvestment sit side by side in marketing plans.

Nothing in a uniqueness objective bans ploughing surplus back into the business.

So the statement is False.

Customers pay when they buy. That payment is sales revenue flowing into the firm.

So the statement is True.

Higher sales usually help profit, but not always.

Heavy discounting, rising input costs, or extra marketing spend can erase the gain — so the link has real limitations.

So the statement is False.

Sales targets are a core marketing objective category because the business needs revenue to operate and to work toward profit.

A plan that skips them leaves out that revenue pillar.

So the statement is True.

Fifty percent share says nothing about costs or margins.

A firm can dominate a market and still lose money if prices sit below unit cost.

Profit needs revenue above the relevant costs, not a share threshold alone.

So the statement is False.

title: Reinvestment Objective Errors
context: Review limitations on the sales-profit link when discounting or costs offset volume gains. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Volume sold through online channels counts toward overall sales objectives.
Sales growth from loyal repeat customers is a sustainable volume source.
Production must be aligned with sales objectives to avoid unmet demand or excess stock.
A temporary sales spike from a campaign still counts toward period volume objectives.
Sales cover variable and fixed production costs when revenue is sufficient.
tactical_explanations:
Online channel volume still counts toward overall sales objectives.

So the statement is True.

Repeat buyers from a loyal base keep volume coming without endlessly hunting new customers.

That repeat flow is a durable source of sales growth when satisfaction holds.

So the statement is True.

If production lags the sales plan, stockouts appear; if it overruns, inventory piles up.

Aligning output with sales targets avoids both traps. Operations and marketing therefore share the same volume number even when their daily tasks differ.

So the statement is True.

A campaign spike still belongs to the period’s sales total.

Objectives usually measure what was sold in the window, including temporary lifts.

So the statement is True.

When revenue is high enough, it covers variable costs first and then contributes toward fixed production costs.

That coverage is why sales matter before any profit line is drawn.

So the statement is True.

title: Repeat Purchase Denials
context: Analyze interrelated marketing objectives that reinforce one another across the customer lifecycle. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profits are unimportant because owners require no return on invested money.
A discounting strategy that maximises unit sales always maximises profit simultaneously.
Profitability objectives conflict with customer satisfaction and cannot coexist.
Marketing staff may compare actual sales to targeted sales each month.
Retained earnings from profit cannot finance marketing campaigns.
tactical_explanations:
Owners put capital at risk and expect a return. Profit is how that return shows up.

Saying profits do not matter because owners need no return reverses the textbook reason for profitability objectives.

So the statement is False.

Maximising unit sales with deep discounts can destroy margin.

More units at a loss do not maximise profit. Volume and profit can pull in opposite directions under aggressive price cuts, which is why “always maximises profit simultaneously” fails.

So the statement is False.

Satisfaction and profitability reinforce each other when loyal customers buy again at viable margins.

They are not mutually exclusive objectives.

So the statement is False.

Month-end actual-versus-target sales checks track progress on volume goals.

So the statement is True.

Retained earnings are profit kept in the business. Firms routinely use that internal finance for campaigns and brand work.

So the statement is False.

title: Promotion-Only Differentiation
context: Review loyalty as an outcome when satisfaction leads customers to buy the product again. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher sales figures never contribute to profit under any market condition.
Increasing sales in export markets can be a marketing objective for growth.
Sales volume objectives may be adjusted after market analysis reveals demand limits.
Profit is recorded before sales revenue is earned from customers.
A price reduction might raise unit sales while affecting revenue per unit.
tactical_explanations:
In ordinary trading conditions, higher sales expand the revenue base that can support profit once costs are covered.

The claim that higher sales never help profit under any condition is too absolute.

So the statement is False.

Export growth is a legitimate sales objective when the firm wants volume outside the home market.

So the statement is True.

If demand analysis shows a ceiling, managers can revise volume targets downward rather than chase an unreachable number.

Sales objectives are planning tools, not fixed forever.

So the statement is True.

Profit is calculated after sales revenue is earned and costs are matched against it.

You do not book profit before customers have paid.

So the statement is False.

Cutting price often lifts units sold while shrinking revenue per unit.

Both effects matter when you read the sales and profit outcomes together.

So the statement is True.

title: Share Maintenance Denials
context: Analyze unique selling propositions that position a product as better than the rest in buyers' minds. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Marketing success is judged only by share gains with no regard to profit.
Profit reinvestment means paying all revenue to suppliers immediately.
Profitability requires sales to fall so that costs can be eliminated.
Owners' invested money is reimbursed through promotional reach metrics.
Sales are important because they provide the funds to cover production costs and profit.
tactical_explanations:
Share gains are one competitiveness signal, but marketing success is also judged on sales, satisfaction, and profit.

Ignoring profit while chasing share alone is not how the chapter frames success. A firm can buy share with unsustainable discounting and still fail the wider objective set.

So the statement is False.

Reinvestment means keeping profit inside the firm for future use — not handing every euro of revenue straight to suppliers.

Paying suppliers is a cost settlement, not retained earnings.

So the statement is False.

Profitability needs sales revenue above costs. Driving sales down to “eliminate costs” does not create profit; it shrinks the revenue base.

So the statement is False.

Promotional reach metrics track awareness or exposure. They do not reimburse owners for invested capital.

That reimbursement comes from profit.

So the statement is False.

Sales bring in the money that covers production costs and, if enough remains, profit.

So the statement is True.

title: Volume Profit Assumptions
context: Review market share as a relative measure rather than an absolute sales total alone. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Volume targets at retail level roll up to manufacturer sales objectives.
A USP guarantees profit without regard to sales volume or costs.
A business may prioritise sales growth when entering a new customer segment.
Profitability objectives apply only when the firm has no competitors.
Retained profit must be distributed entirely to creditors each year.
tactical_explanations:
Retail sell-through feeds manufacturer shipments. Volume targets at retail therefore roll up into the manufacturer’s sales objectives.

So the statement is True.

A USP helps the product stand out and can support loyalty, but profit still needs units sold at margins that clear costs.

Uniqueness on its own does not print a surplus. A distinctive offer that barely sells, or sells only after deep discounting, can still miss the profit target.

So the statement is False.

Entering a new segment often starts with a sales-growth push to build presence before later tightening margin goals.

Prioritising volume there is a normal marketing choice.

So the statement is True.

Profitability objectives apply with many rivals or with few.

So the statement is False.

Retained profit stays in the business. It is not an annual mandatory payout to creditors.

Creditors are paid under debt terms; retained earnings finance growth.

So the statement is False.

title: Objective Hierarchy Mistakes
context: Analyze maintaining sales as essential for ongoing revenue to fund business activity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Limitations on the sales-profit link mean higher sales always lower profit.
Sales performance relative to plan indicates marketing effectiveness.
Revenue objectives are closely tied to sales volume and selling price.
Profitability is unrelated to marketing because marketing generates only costs.
Maintaining sales during an economic downturn can be a demanding marketing objective.
tactical_explanations:
Limitations mean higher sales do not always raise profit — for example when discounts erase margin.

They do not mean higher sales always lower profit. That flips a caution into an absolute reverse claim the chapter does not make.

So the statement is False.

Comparing actual sales with the plan checks whether marketing delivered the volume it promised.

So the statement is True.

Revenue = price × volume (in simple form). Sales objectives and price decisions therefore sit right next to revenue goals.

So the statement is True.

Marketing does generate costs, but it also generates the sales that fund the business.

Profitability remains a marketing objective precisely because those sales must leave a surplus after costs.

So the statement is False.

Holding volume when demand softens in a downturn is a tough but real sales objective.

Many plans explicitly aim to maintain sales rather than grow them in that phase.

So the statement is True.

title: Customer Needs Neglect
context: Review profitability enabling owners to be reimbursed and the firm to retain funds internally. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sales from repeat purchases reduce dependence on costly new customer acquisition.
A marketing objective to double sales implies a substantial volume increase target.
Sales growth supports the broader aim of making a profit after covering costs.
Trade promotions to retailers may aim to lift sell-through sales volume.
A firm with high customer satisfaction cannot pursue profitability objectives.
tactical_explanations:
Repeat purchases from existing customers cut the need to keep buying expensive new leads.

That saving is one reason satisfaction and loyalty objectives support sales.

So the statement is True.

“Double sales” is a substantial volume (or revenue) stretch target.

So the statement is True.

Sales growth widens the revenue pool. After costs, that is what makes profit possible.

So the statement is True.

Trade promotions aimed at retailers often exist to push sell-through — more units leaving the shelf.

That is a sales-volume play.

So the statement is True.

High satisfaction and profitability routinely sit in the same plan.

Loyal, happy customers can still be served at a margin that reimburses owners. Treating the two objectives as mutually exclusive invents a conflict the chapter does not require.

So the statement is False.

title: Perceived Uniqueness Denials
context: Analyze how businesses set marketing objectives after analysing the markets they wish to operate in. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sales monitoring by region helps allocate marketing resources effectively.
Volume sold is a direct measure of progress on sales-related marketing objectives.
Sales revenue must be earned before profit can be distributed or retained.
A firm may accept lower margin temporarily to achieve a sales volume milestone.
Marketing objectives on sales recognise that businesses need revenues to operate.
tactical_explanations:
Regional sales monitoring helps allocate marketing resources.

So the statement is True.

If the objective is sales, units or revenue sold are the direct progress score.

So the statement is True.

Profit is what remains after sales revenue covers costs.

You earn the revenue first; only then can you distribute or retain a surplus.

So the statement is True.

Launch periods sometimes trade margin for a volume milestone — accept a thinner contribution for a while to hit the sales gate.

That temporary bargain is still a conscious marketing choice, not an accident.

So the statement is True.

Businesses need revenues to operate. Sales objectives exist because that cash inflow has to be planned and monitored.

So the statement is True.

title: Competitiveness Indicator Traps
context: Review the role of customer satisfaction as a marketing objective linked to repeat purchase and loyalty. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profit reinvestment is the same as issuing new share capital to investors.
Higher sales from satisfied loyal customers illustrate interrelated marketing objectives.
Sales targets for a new store opening reflect geographic expansion objectives.
Volume growth without cost control may fail to improve profitability.
Sales covering production costs is sufficient for profit with no margin required.
tactical_explanations:
Issuing new shares brings fresh external capital from investors.

Reinvesting profit keeps earnings already earned inside the firm. Those are different financing routes, even though both can fund growth.

So the statement is False.

Satisfied loyal customers buy again, lifting sales while also advancing satisfaction and loyalty goals.

That cross-link is exactly “interrelated marketing objectives” in action.

So the statement is True.

A new store’s sales target expresses geographic expansion in volume or revenue.

So the statement is True.

Growing units while costs race ahead can leave profit flat or worse.

Volume without cost control does not guarantee a better bottom line.

So the statement is True.

Covering production costs gets you to break-even on those costs. Profit still needs a margin above that coverage.

So the statement is False.

title: Revenue Flow Assertions
context: Analyze how a unique selling proposition supports product differentiation and attracts loyal customers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profitability is a marketing objective because profits reimburse owners for invested money.
Profits can be retained and reinvested in the business for future growth.
Usually the higher the sales figures are, the more profit a business will make, with certain limitations.
Profitability objectives sit alongside satisfaction, differentiation, share, and sales goals.
Marketing success ultimately contributes to profit when revenues exceed relevant costs.
tactical_explanations:
Profitability is a marketing objective because profits reimburse owners for invested money.

So the statement is True.

When earnings stay in the firm, managers can fund capacity, brand, or product work for later growth.

Retained profit is that internal fuel.

So the statement is True.

As a rule of thumb, more sales mean more profit — with the chapter’s limitations on costs, discounts, and mix still applying.

Managers therefore read sales lifts together with margin, not as an automatic profit promise.

So the statement is True.

Profit sits in the same objective set as satisfaction, differentiation, share, and sales.

Plans typically juggle all of them rather than picking only one.

So the statement is True.

When revenues clear the relevant costs, marketing activity has contributed to profit.

That ultimate financial test closes the loop on the other marketing goals.

So the statement is True.

title: Owner Return Misconceptions
context: Review why gaining and maintaining market share indicates a firm's relative competitiveness. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profitability is measured by customer satisfaction scores rather than financial surplus.
Owners expect profits as compensation for the capital they invested in the firm.
Retained profit can finance new equipment without raising external finance.
A profitability target may be expressed as a margin percentage on sales.
Higher sales support profitability when unit margins and costs remain favourable.
tactical_explanations:
Satisfaction scores measure how customers feel. Profitability is a financial surplus after costs.

Useful as both are, they are not the same yardstick, and substituting one for the other misreads the objective set.

So the statement is False.

Owners expect profits as compensation for invested capital.

So the statement is True.

Keeping profit inside the firm can buy new equipment without a new loan or share issue.

That is retained earnings at work.

So the statement is True.

A target such as “12% margin on sales” is a profitability objective stated as a percentage of revenue.

So the statement is True.

If unit margins hold and costs stay in check, lifting sales lifts profit.

When those conditions break, the support weakens — which is why the link is conditional, not magical.

So the statement is True.

title: Satisfaction Sales Interlink
context: Analyze the importance of maintaining or increasing sales to cover production costs and earn profit. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profit objectives acknowledge that sales alone do not guarantee profit in every case.
Marketing campaigns are assessed partly on whether they improve profitable sales.
Reinvestment of profit supports long-term marketing and production capacity.
Profitability is important because it sustains the business for owners and reinvestment.
Higher sales always eliminate the need to reinvest profit in the business.
tactical_explanations:
Profit objectives exist partly because sales volume alone can disappoint.

So the statement is True.

Campaign reviews routinely ask whether the lift was profitable sales, not just noisy traffic.

So the statement is True.

Ploughed-back profit can fund plant, systems, or marketing capacity that supports later periods.

So the statement is True.

Without profit, owners lose their return and the firm lacks internal funds to renew itself.

That dual role is why profitability matters in the marketing objective set.

So the statement is True.

Strong sales do not remove the need to reinvest. Capacity, brands, and product lines still need funding over time.

Higher sales can create the profit that makes reinvestment possible — they do not replace that reinvestment step.

So the statement is False.

title: USP Loyalty Connection
context: Review profitability as a marketing objective and its link to reimbursing owners and reinvestment. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A firm may reject unprofitable volume that fails margin thresholds.
Profit objectives are met when advertising spending equals total revenue.
Owners receive reimbursement only through wages, never through profit.
Cost increases can offset sales growth and limit profit improvement.
Profit retained in the business reduces dependence on external borrowing for expansion.
tactical_explanations:
Managers can refuse unprofitable volume that fails margin thresholds rather than chase empty sales.

So the statement is True.

Equating advertising spend with total revenue only describes a cost ratio.

It never shows whether anything remains after all costs — so it cannot, by itself, meet a profitability objective.

A firm could spend every euro of revenue on ads and still report a loss.

So the statement is False.

Owners can take profit as their return on capital. Wages pay labour, not ownership reimbursement.

Collapsing profit into wages misstates how owners are compensated.

So the statement is False.

A cost spike can cancel the benefit of higher sales and leave profit little improved.

That is one of the standard limitations on the sales–profit link.

So the statement is True.

Retained earnings reduce how much the firm must borrow for expansion.

Internal profit keeps the balance sheet less dependent on outside lenders.

So the statement is True.

title: Relative Importance Measures
context: Analyze how customer satisfaction interrelates with other marketing objectives such as sales and loyalty. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Marketing objectives include profitability because owners need returns on investment.
Discounting that raises sales volume may reduce profitability per unit sold.
Profit measurement follows revenue from sales minus the costs of production and marketing.
A profitability review examines whether marketing spend generated adequate returns.
Profitability and market share move in opposite directions in every case.
tactical_explanations:
Marketing objectives include profitability because owners need returns on investment.

So the statement is True.

A discount that moves more units can shrink contribution per unit.

Volume up, profit per sale down — both can happen at once.

So the statement is True.

Profit is typically sales revenue minus production and marketing costs.

That arithmetic is how the surplus is measured.

So the statement is True.

Reviewing whether marketing spend earned an adequate return is a profitability check on the campaign mix.

So the statement is True.

Share and profit sometimes move together and sometimes trade off — for example when share is bought with heavy discounting.

They do not move in opposite directions in every case, so the absolute claim fails.

So the statement is False.

title: Production Cost Coverage
context: Review how product differentiation can rest on product characteristics or on promotion and customer perception. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Satisfied loyal customers who buy repeatedly can improve lifetime profitability.
Profit reinvestment may fund brand-building that supports future differentiation.
Higher sales figures usually mean more profit, though limitations such as rising costs apply.
Profitability objectives encourage attention to cost coverage, not only gross revenue.
Owners may withdraw part of profit as income while retaining the rest in the business.
tactical_explanations:
Satisfied loyal customers who buy repeatedly can improve lifetime profitability.

So the statement is True.

Retained profit can pay for brand-building that later supports differentiation and a clearer USP.

So the statement is True.

Usually more sales mean more profit, subject to rising costs, mix shifts, or discount pressure.

The chapter states the positive link with those limitations attached rather than as an unconditional law.

So the statement is True.

Profit objectives push managers to cover costs properly, not just to celebrate gross revenue.

So the statement is True.

Owners may take some profit as personal income and leave the rest inside as retained earnings.

Both uses are ordinary.

So the statement is True.

title: Profit Limitation Awareness
context: Analyze why building a brand supports the creation of a unique selling proposition. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A marketing plan should consider whether sales targets are profit-compatible.
Profit from one product line can subsidise marketing investment in another line.
Profitability is linked to sales because sales provide the revenue base for profit calculation.
Retained earnings from profit strengthen the firm's internal finance for marketing.
A firm pursuing share at the expense of margin may temporarily reduce profitability.
tactical_explanations:
Sales targets should be checked for profit compatibility.

So the statement is True.

Surplus from a strong line can fund marketing on a developing line.

Cross-subsidy inside the portfolio is a normal use of profit.

So the statement is True.

Sales create the revenue figure that profit calculations start from once costs are deducted.

Without that sales base there is simply no surplus line to discuss. That is why profitability objectives stay linked to sales performance even when managers also watch margin and mix.

So the statement is True.

Retained earnings are internal finance. Marketing initiatives often draw on that stock of past profit.

So the statement is True.

Buying share with thin margins can cut near-term profitability on purpose while the firm builds position.

So the statement is True.

title: Integrated Marketing Objective Review
context: Review how market share reflects a business position relative to competitors in the same market. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profit objectives motivate efficient use of marketing budgets.
Limitations on the sales-profit link include unfavourable changes in unit costs.
Profitability allows owners to be compensated while the firm retains funds for growth.
Marketing staff may track gross profit by product to align with profitability objectives.
A USP supporting premium pricing can improve profitability if costs are controlled.
tactical_explanations:
Profit objectives motivate careful use of marketing budgets.

So the statement is True.

If unit costs rise unfavourably, extra sales may not lift profit.

That cost move is one clear limitation on the sales–profit link.

So the statement is True.

Profit can pay owners while still leaving funds inside for growth.

Compensation and retention can share the same surplus.

So the statement is True.

Tracking gross profit by product shows which lines carry the profitability objective and which drag it.

So the statement is True.

A USP that supports a premium price improves profit when costs stay controlled under that price.

Differentiation then feeds the financial objective directly instead of living only in the brand story.

So the statement is True.

title: Closing Objective Distinctions
context: Analyze the relationship between higher sales figures and profitability within stated limitations. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profit reinvestment in production capacity can support future sales growth.
Profitability is a stated marketing objective in the textbook marketing overview.
Sales must cover production costs before any profit can be recorded.
Owners reinvest profit when they expect future returns from expanded operations.
A decline in profitability despite stable sales may reflect higher input costs.
tactical_explanations:
Ploughing profit into capacity can raise what the firm can sell later.

Reinvestment today supports sales growth tomorrow.

So the statement is True.

Profitability is listed among the textbook marketing objectives.

So the statement is True.

Until sales cover production costs, there is no profit left to record.

Cost coverage comes first in the arithmetic.

So the statement is True.

Owners reinvest profit when they expect better future returns from expanded operations — new capacity, new markets, or stronger brands that should pay back later.

That forward-looking bet is why retained earnings are not only an accounting leftover.

So the statement is True.

Stable sales with falling profit often point to higher input costs squeezing the margin.

Volume held steady while the cost line moved.

So the statement is True.

title: Final Marketing Goals Assessment
context: Review why dissatisfied customers are unlikely to buy a product again. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profit targets may be set annually alongside sales and share objectives.
Marketing that attracts profitable customer segments supports profitability objectives.
Retained profit is internally generated finance for marketing initiatives.
The relationship between sales and profit is positive in general but not without exceptions.
Profitability objectives remind managers that revenue growth must exceed cost growth.
tactical_explanations:
Profit targets may be set annually alongside sales and share objectives.

So the statement is True.

Attracting segments that buy at healthy margins advances the profitability objective, not only awareness.

So the statement is True.

Retained profit is finance generated inside the firm — ready for marketing initiatives without a new loan.

So the statement is True.

In general, more sales help profit, but exceptions exist when costs or discounts intervene.

Positive on average, not guaranteed in every instance.

So the statement is True.

Profitability objectives force the comparison: did revenue growth outrun cost growth?

Without that reminder, volume alone can look like success while the surplus shrinks underneath.

So the statement is True.

title: Comprehensive Objective Assertions
context: Analyze how a unique selling proposition makes a product seem special, unique, or better than alternatives. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained profit cannot support production capacity expansion.
A profitability objective is fulfilled when the firm has the most employees.
A business may analyse contribution margin per unit to support profit objectives.
Marketing that raises sales with rising costs always increases profit.
Profitability is excluded when businesses analyse customer wishes and needs.
tactical_explanations:
Retained profit is a standard source of funds for expanding production capacity.

Saying it cannot support that expansion is incorrect.

So the statement is False.

Headcount is not a profitability measure.

Having the most employees does not fulfil a profit objective.

So the statement is False.

Contribution margin per unit shows how each sale helps cover fixed costs and profit.

So the statement is True.

Sales up with costs rising faster can leave profit unchanged or lower.

“Always increases profit” is the false absolute — marketing that buys volume with expensive acquisition or heavy discounting can grow the top line while the bottom line stalls.

So the statement is False.

Analysing wishes and needs does not exclude profitability.

Market-oriented work still aims for a surplus; customer focus and profit sit together.

So the statement is False.

title: Late-Stage USP and Share Cases
context: Review the marketing objective of maintaining sales volume to generate revenue. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profits reimburse owners and can be ploughed back into the business per the text.
Marketing objectives on profit recognise limitations when discounting erodes margins.
Higher sales volume increases the revenue pool from which profit is calculated after costs.
Profit retention funds improvements that may later support customer satisfaction.
Profits are important only for tax purposes and not for reinvestment.
tactical_explanations:
Profits reimburse owners and can be ploughed back into the business.

So the statement is True.

When discounting erodes margins, sales growth may not deliver the profit target.

Profit objectives have to recognise that limitation.

So the statement is True.

Higher volume enlarges the revenue pool from which profit is calculated after costs.

More units do not guarantee a bigger surplus, but they do widen the starting revenue figure managers then challenge with cost lines.

So the statement is True.

Keeping profit inside can fund improvements — service, quality, or experience — that later lift satisfaction.

So the statement is True.

Profits matter for reinvestment and owner return, not only for tax line items.

Reducing their importance to tax alone is wrong.

So the statement is False.

title: Terminal Profit and Sales Review
context: Analyze how retained profit from higher sales can be reinvested in the business. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profitability assessment includes whether marketing achieved cost-effective sales growth.
Owners' invested money is reimbursed through profits earned from successful operations.
A firm may delay profit growth while investing heavily in brand and USP development.
Profit reinvestment is a strategic use of earnings kept within the business.
Limitations on sales-driven profit include simultaneous increases in marketing expenditure.
tactical_explanations:
Did marketing grow sales in a cost-effective way? That question is part of profitability assessment.

So the statement is True.

Successful operations earn profits that reimburse owners for the money they invested.

So the statement is True.

A firm may delay profit growth while investing heavily in brand and USP development.

Managers sometimes accept that delay deliberately because differentiation built now is meant to support margins later.

So the statement is True.

Profit reinvestment is a strategic use of earnings kept inside the business.

So the statement is True.

If marketing expenditure rises with sales, the extra cost can limit how much profit the volume creates.

That simultaneous spend increase is one stated limitation.

So the statement is True.

title: Marketing Case 100
context: Review the interdependence of customer satisfaction, differentiation, market share, sales, and profitability objectives. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profitability and sales objectives are interrelated but not identical measures.
Marketing performance should ultimately contribute to sustainable profitability.
Retained profit strengthens the balance sheet for future marketing campaigns.
Profit per unit may fall even when total sales volume rises if prices are cut sharply.
Marketing objectives exclude profitability whenever sales volume targets are set.
tactical_explanations:
Sales track volume or revenue; profitability tracks the surplus after costs. Related, not identical.

So the statement is True.

Over time marketing is judged partly on whether it supports sustainable profitability — not only on short bursts of awareness or traffic.

A campaign that fills the funnel but never clears cost will fail that longer test even if sales noise looked healthy for a week.

So the statement is True.

Retained profit strengthens equity and cash capacity for later campaigns.

A healthier balance sheet funds the next push.

So the statement is True.

Sharp price cuts can raise units while cutting profit per unit — total volume up, unit profit down.

So the statement is True.

Setting sales volume targets does not kick profitability out of the objective set.

Plans usually carry both.

So the statement is False.

title: Product Orientation Versus Market Orientation
context: Review how product-oriented and market-oriented businesses differ in where they place initial emphasis when developing offerings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A product-oriented business first analyses customers' needs and wants before defining product specifications.
A product-oriented business focuses on the product and its specifications first and later thinks about how to sell it.
A market-oriented business will first analyse customers' needs and wants and then tailor products to fulfil these requirements.
Product-oriented and market-oriented businesses may pursue identical marketing objectives even when their strategic starting points differ.
A product-oriented business mainly relies on the quality of the features of the product to be successful in the market.
tactical_explanations:
Product orientation starts with the product and its specifications.

Needs-and-wants analysis first is the market-oriented sequence, not the product-oriented one. Swapping those starting points mislabels the orientation.

So the statement is False.

A product-oriented business focuses on the product and its specifications first, then on how to sell it.
